MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "multiple myeloma"
- Say → "Lateral X-ray of the skull of an older adult. There are **multiple, osteolytic** lesions with **well-defined** margins and **no sclerotic rim**: punched-out lesions. So this is a **malignant** picture."
- Then → "Over 40 my differential is **myeloma, metastasis, lymphoma**. I would ask for CBC (complete blood count), ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate), calcium, creatinine, **serum and urine protein electrophoresis**, then marrow biopsy; a **skeletal survey or whole-body MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)**, not a bone scan."

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **>50, male · spine, ribs, skull, pelvis (red marrow) · punched-out, no rim, cold scan · sheets of plasma cells · chemotherapy; surgeon fixes**

### 1 Definition
- Multiple myeloma → **malignant** · hematopoietic origin → monoclonal **plasma cells** secreting **M-protein** · one lesion = **plasmacytoma**
- **Most common primary malignancy of bone** (Campbell)

| Plasma cell disorder | What it is |
|---|---|
| **MGUS** (monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance) | M-protein only, no damage · ≈3% over 50 · ≈1% a year → myeloma (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **Smouldering myeloma** | Marrow plasma cells + M-protein, **no lytic lesions** · ≈10% a year progress early (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **Solitary plasmacytoma** | One lesion, marrow ≤10% · **50–75% become myeloma** (Miller) |
| **Multiple myeloma** | Clonal plasma cells + **end-organ damage (CRAB)** |
| **Osteosclerotic myeloma (POEMS)** | Rare sclerotic variant · polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, M-protein, skin changes |

PITFALL — how common is MGUS?
- Prof Abosena → 1% over 50 · OKU → ≈3%, and 1% a year progress
- Say → "MGUS in about 3% over 50; about **1% a year** turn into myeloma"

### 2 Origin
- **Hematopoietic** → B lymphocyte → **plasma cell**; genetic hits decide progression
- Cytokines raise **RANKL** → osteoclasts · DKK-1 → **osteoblasts suppressed** → resorption **without** new bone → lytic film, cold scan (OKU Tumors 4)

### 3 Incidence
- Age → **exception**: peak **5th–7th decades** (Campbell) · Sex → male ≈ **2 : 1** · more common in **black** patients (Prof Abosena)
- Rank → **2nd commonest malignant bone tumour**, 1st primary (Handbook)

### 4 Sites
- Longitudinal → any **red marrow**; long bones begin **centrally** · Transverse → central
- Special → **spine > ribs > pelvis**, skull, proximal femur, humerus · Never → rare distal to elbow and knee (Campbell) · groups → multiple, cold, small round-cell → 1 Differential

- Forearm bones, punched-out lesions (Prof Abosena)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined (no rim) | thinning | multiple | **malignant** |

### 5 Clinical presentation
| Local | Systemic | Complications by location |
|---|---|---|
| **Bone pain**, worse at night (75%); mimics sciatica · **pathological fracture** | Anaemia, infection, bleeding, hyperviscosity · hypercalcaemia ≈30% (OKU Tumors 4) | Spine → **cord compression** (up to 5%) · ribs → dyspnoea |

- **Systemic** → **CRAB** = hyper**C**alcaemia (>10.5 mg/dL) · **R**enal failure (creatinine >2 mg/dL) · **A**naemia (Hb <10 g/dL) · **B**one lesions (OKU Tumors 4)
- "Elderly + back pain + **anaemia** → myeloma until proved otherwise" (Prof Abosena) · kidney → light-chain casts, amyloid

### 6 Imaging
| Frame A step | Myeloma |
|---|---|
| Behavior | **Purely osteolytic** · rare sclerotic variant (POEMS) |
| Margins | **Well-defined, no sclerotic rim** · untreated may be permeative |
| Cortical reaction | **Endosteal scalloping** (diffuse myelomatosis), fracture; sometimes "ballooned" |
| Special signs | **Punched-out** skull ("pepper pot"); thin rim **after** treatment; **mini-brain** vertebra on T2 MRI (Greenspan) |

- Punched-out skull, 60-year-old woman (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| skull | — | osteolytic | well-defined (no rim) | destruction | multiple · punched-out | **malignant** |

- Pelvis, multiple lytic lesions (lecture context) (Prof Abosena)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pelvis | — | osteolytic | ill-defined (moth-eaten) | destruction | multiple | **malignant** |

- Long bones: A mature lesion, B permeative, C fracture (OKU Tumors 4)

| Film | Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | thinning | none | **malignant** |
| B | diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined (permeative) | thinning | none | **malignant** |
| C | diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined | destruction | pathological fracture | **malignant** |

- Endosteal scalloping, distal femur and elbow, 65-year-old (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined | thinning | endosteal scalloping · multiple | **malignant** |

- Treated femoral lesions with a thin rim, 4 years apart (OKU Tumors 4)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined (sclerotic rim) | thinning | multiple · treated | **malignant** |

| Test | Role in myeloma |
|---|---|
| **Bone scan** | **Cold**: detects only 35–60% of lesions → not in the work-up (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **Skeletal survey** | Spine, humeri, femora, skull, chest, pelvis → ≈80% show a lesion |
| Whole-body low-dose CT (computed tomography) | Finds lesions in 25% with a negative survey |
| **Whole-body MRI** | Most sensitive; **first-line for suspected solitary plasmacytoma**; STIR (short tau inversion recovery) bright |
| FDG PET (positron emission tomography)/CT | Best for residual disease after treatment |

- Punched-out skull and a poor bone scan, same patient (OKU Tumors 4)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| skull | — | osteolytic | well-defined (no rim) | destruction | multiple · cold on bone scan | **malignant** |

- Sagittal MRI spine, T1 and STIR (lecture context) (Prof Abosena)
- Mini-brain sign, axial T2 MRI of a lumbar vertebra (Greenspan)
- FDG PET/CT: femoral and cervical lesions (OKU Tumors 4)

CLINICAL PEARL — why the scan is cold
- Osteoblasts are suppressed, the scan marks new bone → it misses most lesions → **skeletal survey or whole-body MRI** → 2 Cold lesions (OKU Tumors 4)

**Plasmacytoma and the sclerotic variant**
- Plasmacytoma → destruction + soft-tissue mass; MRI T1 intermediate, T2 bright

- Solitary plasmacytoma of the ischium, CT angiogram and CT, 79-year-old (Greenspan)
- Plasmacytoma of the proximal femur, coronal MRI, 53-year-old (Greenspan)
- POEMS, sclerotic myeloma on sagittal CT (OKU Tumors 4)

### 7 Labs
| Test | Finding |
|---|---|
| CBC · ESR | Refractory anaemia, pancytopenia · **high ESR** |
| Chemistry | Calcium, creatinine, uric acid, albumin, β2-microglobulin |
| **Serum + urine protein electrophoresis** | **Monoclonal spike** · reversed albumin : globulin ratio |
| Serum free light chains · urine | Light-chain myeloma · **Bence Jones** proteins |
| **Bone marrow** | Clonal plasma cells; **>60% → treat as myeloma** even without CRAB (OKU Tumors 4) |

- **Specific** → Polyclonal rise → liver disease, chronic infection, **not myeloma** · IgM monoclonal → Waldenström, lymphoma (Prof Abosena)

- Monoclonal spike on electrophoresis (lecture context) (Prof Abosena)

PITFALL — major and minor criteria
- Handbook, Prof Abosena → old major/minor criteria (marrow >30%, plasmacytoma, Bence Jones >1 g/24 h · lytic lesions, low M-protein, low Igs) · OKU → clonal plasma cells + **CRAB**
- Say → "Clonal plasma cells in the marrow **plus CRAB**; I know the old major/minor scheme"

### 8 Biopsy
- **Modality** → Marrow aspirate or trephine (sternum, iliac crest), or core biopsy of the lesion · **sheets of plasma cells**: eccentric "clock-face" nucleus, perinuclear halo
- **CD138, CD38, CD56** positive, CD19/CD20 negative (OKU Tumors 4) · exclude lymphoma (CD20 +) and osteomyelitis (polyclonal plasma cells)

### 9 Differential diagnosis
- **Location groups** → By location → red marrow, diaphyseal and flat bones → 1 Differential · by cortex → non-expansile, endosteal scalloping
- **Histology groups** → By cell → **small round cells**: lymphoma, metastasis, Ewing in the young · **Special DD** → the mimic → **metastasis**, hyperparathyroidism, osteoporosis

| Myeloma vs | Separates them |
|---|---|
| Metastasis | Electrophoresis, biopsy; pedicles spared early; cold scan |
| Hyperparathyroidism | PTH (parathormone) high, normal electrophoresis, hot scan |
| Eosinophilic granuloma | Punched-out skull in the **young** |
| Osteoporosis | Diffuse osteolysis → electrophoresis |

### 10 Grading
- Own staging, not Enneking or AJCC → **ISS** (International Staging System) · Durie–Salmon (lesions, Hb, calcium, M-protein, kidney)

| ISS | β2-microglobulin | Albumin | Median survival |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | <3.5 mg/L | ≥3.5 g/dL | 62 months |
| II | Neither I nor III | — | 45 months |
| III | >5.5 mg/L | Any | 29 months |

- Revised ISS → adds LDH (lactate dehydrogenase) and high-risk genetics (OKU Tumors 4)

### 11 Treatment
- MGUS, smouldering → **observation** · solitary plasmacytoma → **radiotherapy 40–45 Gy**, control up to 92% (OKU Tumors 4)
- **Systemic** → Myeloma → **systemic** (bortezomib, lenalidomide or thalidomide + steroid; stem-cell transplant if <65 and fit) · **zoledronic acid**, **denosumab non-inferior** (OKU Tumors 4) · radiotherapy 8 Gy for pain
- **Malignant local** → Surgeon → **biopsy**, prophylactic fixation (Mirels), fractures, spinal decompression · stabilise the **entire bone** (nail or plate, then radiotherapy) · large defect → curettage + PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate) · head/neck → **arthroplasty**
- Radiotherapy **2–3 weeks** after surgery, when the wound has healed (Campbell)

- Proximal femur: CT, embolization, long Gamma nail, histology (Campbell)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined (no rim) | thinning | multiple | **malignant** |

- Humeral fracture, interlocking nail (lecture context) (Prof Abosena)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined | destruction | pathological fracture | **malignant** |

CLINICAL PEARL — myeloma bleeds
- **Extremely vascular** → 3.5 L lost in 10 minutes opening one humerus · never operate **without blood** (≈6 units) and **ICU (intensive care unit) backup** (Prof Abosena)
- Medicine first; operate now only for femoral neck or spine fracture, impending femoral fracture (Prof Abosena)

PITFALL — denosumab and embolization in myeloma
- Prof Abosena → no role for denosumab or embolization · OKU → denosumab non-inferior; Campbell embolizes before fixation
- Say → "Zoledronic acid or denosumab for skeletal events; embolization may be tried, but blood and ICU are the real safety"

### 12 Prognosis & complications
- **Tumour-specific** → Complicatio

11.02.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "bone metastasis"
- Say → "AP X-ray of the femur of an adult. There is a **diaphyseal, central, osteolytic** lesion with **ill-defined** margins. The cortex shows **destruction** with a **pathological fracture**. So this is a **malignant** lesion."
- Then → "Over 40 my differential is **metastasis, myeloma, lymphoma**, then a primary sarcoma. I would do the **unknown-primary work-up**, then biopsy **before** I fix."

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **>40 · spine, pelvis, proximal femur · lytic (kidney, thyroid) / blastic (prostate) · epithelial cells · fix the whole bone, embolize kidney**

### 1 Definition
- Bone metastasis → **malignant** · secondary carcinoma deposit · **commonest malignancy treated by orthopaedic surgeons**; bone metastases in 50–80% at death (Campbell)
- Bone → 3rd site of metastasis after **lung and liver**

### 2 Origin
- Spread by **Batson's valveless vertebral venous plexus** → spine, pelvis, ribs, girdles (Miller) · **vicious cycle** → PTHrP → RANKL → osteoclasts → growth factors → tumour grows

| Primary | Point |
|---|---|
| **Breast, prostate** (commonest) · lung · kidney · thyroid | "BLT with a Kosher Pickle" (Miller) |
| Unknown primary → **lung, kidney** | (Campbell) |
| Others → GI tract, liver, colon | — |

### 3 Incidence
- Age → **>40**; exception → neuroblastoma <5 years (Handbook) · Sex → follows the primary · Rank → **commonest malignant lesion of bone** → 1 Incidence

### 4 Sites
- **Longitudinal** → Metaphyseal or diaphyseal, **Transverse** → central or **cortical** (lung "cookie bite") · **proximal femur** = commonest pathological fracture (Miller)
- **Special sites** → **Spine** commonest, then pelvis and femur · distal to elbow or knee → **lung** most likely (Campbell)

PITFALL — "metastasis below the knee = renal"
- Nagah p19 → renal · Campbell → **lung** most likely; Greenspan shows renal tibial deposits (possible, not first)
- Say → "Acral and below-knee metastasis → **lung first**, then kidney and breast"

### 5 Clinical presentation
| Local | Systemic | Complications by location |
|---|---|---|
| **Pain**: constant, at night · fracture, often after warning pain | Signs of the primary · hypercalcaemia up to 20%; Ca >14 mg/dL urgent (OKU Tumors 4) | Spine → radiculopathy, cord, cauda equina · proximal femur → fracture |

- Known carcinoma, even long ago → new bone lesion = **metastasis** most likely (Campbell)
- **Complications** → **Skeletal-related events (SREs)** → pathological fracture, cord compression, radiotherapy to bone, surgery to bone (OKU Tumors 4)

### 6 Imaging
| Pattern | Primary |
|---|---|
| **Lytic** | **Kidney, thyroid** (purely lytic) · lung · GI · breast (usually) (Campbell) |
| **Blastic** | **Prostate** · breast sometimes (Campbell) |
| **Mixed** | Breast, lung |
| Expansile, "blown-out" | Kidney, thyroid (Greenspan) |
| Cortical "cookie bite" | Lung |

- Bone scan → **hot** in most, the best screen; falsely negative in some renal carcinoma · film normal until 30–50% lost · whole-spine MRI → non-contiguous deposits

PITFALL — the Handbook's "sclerotic thyroid" and "cold breast"
- Handbook → thyroid sclerotic, breast cold · Campbell → thyroid and kidney **purely lytic**; breast usually lytic and hot

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | destruction | medial cortex involved | **benign active** |

- The film above is a **haemangioma**: "minimum Mirels score of 9" even without pain → the score used outside metastasis (Matcuk 2025)

11.04.4.b:
- **Subjective**, poorly reproducible · made **before** modern bisphosphonates; **overestimates** risk · few myeloma lesions in the series · CT rigidity analysis more accurate (OKU Tumors 4)

PITFALL — Mirels for every lesion?
- Prof Abosena → benign and malignant · Mirels' paper → **metastatic disease in long bones** (Campbell)
- Say → "Designed for long-bone metastases; others use it for myeloma and lymphoma; for benign lesions it is only a guide"

11.05.t: Impending vs Actual Pathological Fracture — Fixation Principles
11.05.b:
### Why fix before it breaks
- Prophylactic fixation → less blood loss, **shorter stay**, more discharges home, **more walking** (Miller) · completed fracture → worse survival

- Lung metastasis, distal femur: nail + PMMA (OKU Tumors 4)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined | destruction | none | **malignant** |

- Renal metastasis, proximal femur: fixation cancelled, then fracture (Campbell)

### The principles
- Diagnosis first → first lesion biopsied; renal, thyroid embolized · **immediate full weight bearing** · **durable** → some live years
- **Whole-bone protection** → long IM (intramedullary) nail; **long stem only if distal lesions** (Campbell) · **cement** → lesions rarely heal (OKU Tumors 4)
- Load-bearing nail or arthroplasty over plates · radiotherapy to the whole field **2–3 weeks** after surgery (Campbell)

| Site | Choice |
|---|---|
| Femoral head / neck | **Cemented hemiarthroplasty**; fixation fails (OKU Tumors 4) |
| Inter- / subtrochanteric | Long cephalomedullary nail, else proximal femoral replacement |
| Femoral shaft · distal femur | Long IM nail ± cement · plate + cement or replacement |
| Proximal humerus | <50% loss → curettage + PMMA ± plate; >50% → endoprosthesis |
| Humeral shaft | **IM nail** (radiosensitive) · plate + PMMA (kidney) |
| Acetabulum | Harrington types → cement, pins, cage + cemented cup |

- Femoral neck metastasis: failed nail vs cemented hemiarthroplasty (OKU Tumors 4)
- Humeral diaphyseal metastasis, antegrade IM nail (OKU Tumors 4)
- Prostate metastasis, proximal femoral shaft fracture (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | mixed | ill-defined | destruction | pathological fracture | **malignant** |

- Pathological fractures in general → 12 Pathological fractures

CLINICAL PEARL — the patient may outlive the implant
- A lung-cancer patient lived over a decade with many revisions → build the construct **as durable as possible** (OKU Tumors 4)
